decisions.statement: The ios-app pages read here are the TypeScript pages akasha has.
An app is named by the slug its own page carries.
An app slug no page carries is answered as a refusal as well as thrown.
A script an app names by slug is answered as the file holding that script.
The map of iOS apps is read from disk only on the first call in a process.
An app carries where its own page is.
A repo path with no colon is taken to name the code repo.
The web-env-path a page states is kept as its slash-separated segments.
Whether an app bakes a ring credential is read from the scripts its page names.
No app slug is written here to say which app bakes a ring credential.
A page naming two ring credential scripts is refused rather than answered by the first.
The page carrying a script's slug is asked of the index rather than swept for.
The file holding a script is the `shell` file beside that script's page.
No file name ending is spelled here to find a script.
An app carries the file making its native sources as well as the file building it.

definition: an iOS app as stated on its ios-app page, with the repo paths it spells
